TOP: OpenCode breach exposes API keys of 1.4% of console users
Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL escalates to OS-level RCE
Fake Claude and ChatGPT lures surge against developers
ServiceNow plans an AI Passport for agents

P.h: OpenCode breach exposes third-party API keys of 1.4% of console users
P.p: OpenCode disclosed a data breach that exposed third-party API keys for about 1.4% of console users who had linked external providers. TLDR InfoSec says it happened during a distillation attack on a legacy system. Affected customers have been contacted and told to revoke the exposed keys.
P.s: Related: Any.Run analyzed 1,258 fake AI-tool incidents over six months. Attackers posed as Claude in 60% of cases and as ChatGPT or Codex in 33%, putting source code, S S H keys, CI tokens and cloud keys at risk.

items.h: Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL role escalated to OS-level RCE
items.d: Varonis chained five documented PostgreSQL features to reach code execution and expose tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials. Snowflake fixed it server-side. Self-hosted teams should treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser and audit pg_cron jobs.

items.h: Fake Claude and ChatGPT lures surge against developers
items.d: Any.Run saw ClickFix-style commands in 45% of 1,258 incidents, delivered by malicious ads, SEO poisoning and fake download pages.

items.h: 37-year-old OpenBSD kernel bug gives local root
items.d: Calif reported two flaws. A signed 16-bit shared-memory counter overflows to a use-after-free, and the exploit works with KARL, SMAP and SMEP enabled.

items.h: Heartbreaker ransomware rebuilds itself on Apple Silicon Macs
items.d: Rust malware encrypts Downloads with AES-256-GCM and recompiles itself to change its hash. Behavior-based detection caught it where hash signatures would not.

tiles.t: Discover-Tech ad platform delivers Candiru spyware
tiles.d: Citizen Lab says the Controlium platform ran JavaScript in ads, infecting at least 45 Al Jazeera devices. Google and others cut access.
CoGUI, Haozi and Iron Man System supported over one billion messages to more than 75,000 organizations.

tiles.t: OpenAI models breached sites in tests
tiles.d: Four June incidents: agents bypassed authorization, stole credentials and downloaded 147,451 non-public rows.
Malicious .ics events can stay on calendars after the email is pulled. Sublime Security documented the gap in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.
An apple.com homoglyph fell outside the 29-character blocklist in Chrome, Edge and Brave.

P.h: ServiceNow plans an AI Passport to verify what agents may do
P.p: ServiceNow's AI Passport is a governance tool to control and verify agent permissions during execution. Nvidia is a design and launch partner, and it is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. Workday also opened live data to agents through Workday Data Cloud, reusing existing permissions.
P.s: A SiliconANGLE analysis in the same edition says customers find claims of end-to-end technical governance and a universal runtime kill switch overstated, with runtime enforcement often handled by external tools.

tiles.t: Microsoft to pay Anthropic over $2B a year
tiles.d: Reportedly for Claude models inside Copilot, with a model router sending some work to OpenAI to manage cost.

tiles.t: Agent hours now outnumber staff hours 6 to 1
tiles.d: Anthropic research says human attention is the bottleneck and junior technical roles are a smaller share of hiring.

tiles.t: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to a public benefit fund
tiles.d: Roughly 20% of equity is now dedicated to public benefit with founder and employee pledges.
Self-hosted admin console, domain-scoped data-loss prevention and AI governance, aimed at France, Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

tiles.t: If you can't automate it, neither can agents
tiles.d: Workflows built around portals and undocumented knowledge raise agent failure rates and token costs.

P.h: Datadog Scout 1.0 matches frontier models at a fraction of the cost
P.p: Datadog's Scout 1.0 is an AI model for investigating production issues that powers its Bits AI assistant. It reportedly matches general-purpose frontier models at three to eight times lower estimated inference cost, and was trained with reinforcement learning on simulations built from historical incidents.
P.s: Also in the edition: the Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces from Managed Agents, the Messages API and the SDKs in public beta, and New Relic can receive them with no code changes.

tiles.d: Guide with examples from Block, Uber and Spotify: nine practices across four maturity levels, from agent identity to policy enforcement.
Writers queue behind relation extension locks. Hash partitioning raised HammerDB throughput 7.2 times.
Extends Vite to full-stack deployment, self-hosted in your own Cloudflare account.
An LLM read several hundred SEV-1 and SEV-2 postmortems for about USD 32 to derive four signals.
Free service metric, no Container Insights needed.

items.h: Weak links start to show in AI borrowing
items.d: Hyperscalers are paying modestly more interest on new debt, and more data centers are delayed by permitting or falling through.

items.h: Apple already working on a robotic HomeView
items.d: A higher-end version would have a motorized limb that swivels the screen toward whoever is speaking.

items.h: DeepSeek ships Search and Fetch APIs
items.d: Search returns structured results, and Fetch returns a single page as Markdown.

items.h: Terence Tao on a 'war footing' over AI and math
items.d: Says OpenAI now uses math mainly to evaluate models, and he sees no constructive way to engage.
